title: Städel Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings that shift attention between a meal, a face, a small object and a public interior.
introduction:
Monet's *Luncheon* gives a family meal a canvas more than two metres high. Juncker's isolated fruit achieves another kind of enlargement: insects and a stone support make an apple or pear seem unusually consequential within a small arrangement. In both cases, an ordinary subject acquires attention through the terms of its presentation.

This selection moves between those scales. A grimace can occupy a whole image; a crowd can become small within a church or exchange hall. Looking at what surrounds a subject, and how much room it is given, helps explain its effect without resorting to a ranking of masterpieces. The entries retain the collection's variety rather than promising one continuous history.
visitNote: These are selected collection works, not a fixed gallery route. Some may be on loan or in storage. Check the Städel’s current object records and visitor information before planning a visit around an individual painting.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: This exhibition catalogue supplies context for Monet’s domestic scene and river view. Its essays and illustrations help place their handling of light beside the later city scenes in this selection.

works.title: The Luncheon
works.credit: Claude Monet. The Luncheon. Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public Domain Mark (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: The bright tablecloth reaches into the foreground, connecting figures who do not all share one action. At over two metres high, the painting gives a private meal the physical scale associated with more public subjects. Monet's dishes, glasses and furnished room therefore deserve more than a quick recognition as domestic accessories: they help hold the large composition together.

works.title: The Lucca Madonna
works.credit: Jan van Eyck. The Lucca Madonna. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The red robe and throne establish authority within a room whose narrow enclosure also feels materially specific. Windows and small furnishings prevent the setting from becoming an indefinite sacred space. Van Eyck brings two registers into contact. Mary can possess ceremonial importance while holding the child close within surroundings that invite attention to ordinary things.

works.title: Ecce Homo
works.credit: Hieronymus Bosch. Here is a Man (Ecce Homo). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The raised platform exposes Christ to a compact crowd below. Architecture separates the figure being presented from the people looking upwards, making public judgment a visible arrangement. Bosch gives the crowd force through its concentration of faces and bright clothing. The scene's hostility is embodied in that unequal relation between exposure and collective attention.

works.title: Young Woman of the Fürleger Family with Loose Hair
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of a Young Fürleger with Loose Hair
works.credit: Albrecht Dürer. Portrait of a Young Fürleger with Loose Hair. Image credit: Albrecht Dürer; Own work; Photographic credit: Sima Farshid. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Portrait_of_a_Young_Woman,_Albrecht_D%C3%BCrer_(1497).jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Lowered eyes and joined hands draw the portrait towards an inward-directed gesture, while carefully described curls spread around the face. Dürer keeps the background restrained enough for those contours to remain important. The quiet pose does not make the surface uneventful. Hair, hands and face each require a different kind of precise attention.

works.title: Helene Roederstein
works.credit: Ottilie Roederstein. Portrait of Helene Roederstein. Image credit: Ottilie Roederstein; Source credit: Städelmuseum, Frankfurt am Main. Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The patterned green dress introduces considerable activity below a comparatively steady face. Joined hands help keep the posture clear, and the pale hat distinguishes the head from the muted background. Ottilie Roederstein allows decoration to remain conspicuous without dispersing the sitter. The portrait's balance depends on different levels of incident across one figure.

works.title: Still Life with Apple and Insects
works.catalogueTitle: Still Life with Apple and Insects
works.credit: Justus Juncker. Still Life with Apple and Insects. Image credit: Justus Juncker; Source credit: https://rkd.nl/nl/explore/images/281212. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A stepped stone support gives the single apple the formality of a displayed object. Tiny insects introduce another scale against which its roundness becomes substantial. Juncker removes the abundance usual in many fruit still lifes. Isolation makes a commonplace subject available for sustained attention to outline, skin and the small life around it.

works.title: Still Life with Pear and Insects
works.catalogueTitle: Still Life with Pear and Insects
works.credit: Justus Juncker. Still Life with Pear and Insects. Image credit: Justus Juncker; Source credit: https://rkd.nl/nl/explore/images/281213. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The pear rises from the stone ledge with a less balanced outline than the neighbouring apple. Butterfly and insect bring delicate forms into contact with fruit and cracked stone. Comparing the two still lifes shows what a repeated setup can reveal: when the surrounding format stays related, a changed contour becomes much more conspicuous.

works.title: A Scholar in His Study
works.credit: Justus Juncker. A Scholar in his Study. Image credit: Justus Juncker; Source credit: https://rkd.nl/nl/explore/images/254454. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Books and accumulated objects establish study as a material practice rather than an invisible mental condition. Light gathers near the table while the room's edges remain less legible. Juncker separates a working area from its crowded surroundings. The painting can show the conditions of concentrated attention without pretending to make the scholar's thoughts available.

works.title: Young Woman in a Wicker Chair
works.catalogueTitle: Young Woman in a Wicker Chair
works.credit: Hanns Katz. Young Woman in a Wicker Chair. Image credit: Hanns Ludwig Katz (1892-1940). Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The chair curves around a narrow body whose hands remain close to the knees. Strong red hair and blue clothing keep the sitter distinct within the compressed arrangement. Katz makes support and ease different questions: a chair may physically contain a figure without making the pose look expansive. That observation need not become a diagnosis of her feelings.

works.title: The Courtyard of the Orphanage in Amsterdam
works.catalogueTitle: The Courtyard of the Orphanage in Amsterdam: Free Period in the Amsterdam Orphanage
works.credit: Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main, Eigentum des Städelschen Museums-Vereins e.V.. Public Domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Repeated uniforms establish an institution, but the girls do not repeat one pose. Some stand, others sit, and their separate pauses remain visible along the shaded building. Liebermann sets that variation against sunlight broken by trees. The courtyard is shared space in which belonging to a group does not erase individual positions or activity.

works.title: Carmencita
works.credit: Lovis Corinth. Carmencita. Image credit: Lovis Corinth. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Broad strokes let dress and setting partly merge, making the surface more restless than a smoothly enclosed portrait would be. Firm accents near the face keep the sitter from disappearing into that activity. Corinth distributes clarity selectively. Recognition is maintained at a few points while the surrounding paint retains the freedom to interrupt stable outlines.

works.title: Conflagration at Night
works.credit: Johann Georg Trautmann. Conflagration at Night. Image credit: Johann Georg Trautmann; Source credit: https://rkd.nl/nl/explore/images/275260. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The fire supplies the illumination that reveals its own damage. Buildings and small figures gather in the blaze's reach, while surrounding darkness limits what can be known. A tree interrupts the glow rather than allowing it to become one continuous bright area. Trautmann turns disaster into a scene whose visibility depends on the destructive event itself.

works.title: Deer in a Japanese Landscape
works.credit: Jean-Bloé Niestlé. Deer in Japanese Landscape. Image credit: Carl Ha; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jean_Blo%C3%A9_Niestl%C3%A9,_Rehe_in_japanischer_Landschaft,_1918.jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Recognisable deer inhabit sharply coloured plants and terrain that resist a single stable perspective. Niestlé makes the animals share space with a conspicuous decorative arrangement. The title should not be treated as proof of a directly observed location. Following colour and curved forms reveals how the setting has been constructed around its living subjects.

works.title: The Bitter Draught
works.credit: Adriaen Brouwer. The Bitter Drunk. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The drink has produced a reaction that interrupts any composed portrait pose. Narrowed eyes, open mouth and the grip on the vessel make an ordinary sensation the whole subject. Brouwer gives attention to a face in transition rather than a settled identity. The grimace is particular enough to carry the scene without a larger anecdote.

works.title: Houses on the Zaan
works.credit: Claude Monet. Häuser am Ufer der Zaan. Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public Domain Mark (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Repeated green façades give the bank a clear rhythm. In the water, their counterparts break into smaller strokes and less stable boundaries. Monet establishes a comparison within one view: buildings retain enough firmness to measure what their reflections lose. The river is therefore an active second description of the shore, not merely a coloured strip beneath it.

works.title: In the Stock Exchange
works.credit: In the Stock Exchange. Ferdinand Brütt; Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Financial activity appears through proximity, turns of bodies and small groups in conversation. Brütt places these difficult-to-read exchanges within a high public interior, giving them a scale beyond the individuals involved. The room establishes an institution while the clustered figures show its operation. The painting cannot disclose each transaction, but it can describe the conditions of exchange.

works.title: Interior of a Baroque Church
works.credit: Interior of a Baroque Church. Johann Ludwig Ernst Morgenstern; Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Arches, columns and the dome connect successive areas of the interior. Small people make the architecture's scale legible without supplying the main event. Morgenstern gives the building several ways of directing attention through rounded forms and layered openings. The space is organised for movement and looking, even when the figures themselves occupy only a small part of it.

works.title: Interior of a Gothic Church
works.credit: Interior of a Gothic Church. Johann Ludwig Ernst Morgenstern; Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Pointed arches and slender supports repeat towards the distant altar. Their upward emphasis differs from the broader rounded forms in Morgenstern's Baroque interior. The pair offers a practical comparison of spatial organisation without requiring a complete account of either architectural style. Follow what repeats and where those repetitions lead the eye.

works.title: Jewish Street in Amsterdam
works.credit: Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public Domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Bright produce makes small transactions distinguishable within the darker crowd. Liebermann describes the neighbourhood through a gathering around a stall rather than a solitary architectural landmark. Brick façades provide continuity behind the changing activity. Public space becomes legible through what people do together, while their individual exchanges remain only partly accessible to a viewer.

works.title: Kitchen Interior with Three Women
works.credit: Kitchen Interior with Three Women. Justus Juncker; Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Sleeves, utensils and ingredients occupy the kitchen's lighter area, directing attention to work at the table. Juncker gives each woman a different gesture within the shared task. Their positions make sense through coordination rather than through a formal group pose. The room is described by its use, with food preparation organising the people and objects together.

closingSections.title: Change scale deliberately
paragraphs: Move between the isolated fruit, Brouwer's face and the large interiors. Notice how surrounding space changes the apparent importance of each subject. Use the Städel's current collection records for display information; this selection is intended for comparison, not as a fixed itinerary.
